changes.reason: Preserve bytes and null bodies in a validated, versioned Redis response format isolated from legacy readers and writers.

kubernetes.reason: The byte-preserving Redis codec reuses the existing Node Redis ISR adapter; no host or connection lifecycle changes.
constraints: Requires a reachable Redis service and the optional ioredis peer.
Uses a cold versioned cache namespace; legacy entries retain their TTL and require coordinated invalidation during mixed-version deployment.
Tests use native Node Request/Response and a synthetic Redis transport; no live Redis or Kubernetes deployment is certified.

aws-lambda.reason: The existing Lambda ISR path uses the same Redis adapter and byte codec; invocation and connection ownership remain with the caller.
constraints: Requires Redis connectivity and caller-managed ioredis connection lifetime in Lambda.
Old and new deployments have separate namespaces and invalidation; rollback can reuse old entries.
Local Lambda handler tests do not certify a deployed AWS environment.

cloudflare.reason: This change is specific to the Node/ioredis Redis adapter and does not provide a Worker-safe durable cache provider.
constraints: Workers must supply a separate Worker-safe IsrCacheStore as required by the existing runtime support contract.
